title: TRAMORNOT: Tramadol versus morphine in postoperative analgesia after laparoscopic abdominal surgery: a randomized controlled trial
official: TRAMORNOT: Tramadol versus morphine in postoperative analgesia after laparoscopic abdominal surgery: a randomized controlled trial
summary: Main objective: The primary objective of this randomized controlled trial is to compare the quality of recovery at 24 hours postoperatively, assessed using the QoR-15 (Quality of Recovery-15) score, in patients receiving multimodal analgesia with either tramadol or morphine during scheduled major laparoscopic abdominal surgery
conditions: Postoperative pain following scheduled major laparoscopic abdominal surgery
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥18 years
2. Scheduled laparoscopic abdominal surgery with an expected operative duration of 2 hours or more
3. Affiliation to the national health insurance system
4. Signed informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
1. Allergy or intolerance to any of the following medications: paracetamol, nefopam, ketoprofen, tramadol, morphine, sufentanil, lidocaine, propofol, ketamine, dexamethasone, or droperidol
2. Patient unable to self-assess pain using a numerical rating scale (0–10) (e.g., due to language barrier)
3. Pregnant or breastfeeding women
4. Patient under legal guardianship, legal protection, or deprived of liberty
5. Contraindication to any of these medications (refer to the Summary of Product Characteristics): paracetamol, ketoprofen, nefopam, tramadol, morphine, sufentanil, lidocaine, propofol, ketamine, dexamethasone, or droperidol
6. Chronic use of monoamine oxidase inhibitors or CYP2D6 inhibitors
7. Chronic preoperative use of level 2 or 3 analgesics
8. Outpatient surgery
9. Surgery requiring postoperative admission to an intensive care unit (ICU)
10. Patient on long-term oxygen therapy
11. Patient with psychiatric disorders
12. Patient with neurodegenerative diseases
